newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - London stocks hit new peak, dollar firm.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - London stocks hit new peak, dollar firm.

text.p: The London stock market hit a new peak in early trading on Monday, buoyed by a record close on Wall Street, while a further burst of festive cheer also boosted the Frankfurt and Paris bourses.
On the currency markets, the dollar was in good form but traded a little below a 45-month peak of 116.20 yen touched in New York on Friday.
Concern about the weakness of the Japanese economy and its sagging stock market put more pressure on the yen, with movements exaggerated by the thinness of end-of-year markets, dealers said.

"Dollar-yen seems to be very well bid. But to be honest, there has not been much action," said a trader at one British bank. "Markets are thin. What will happen is anyone's guess but dollar-yen looks set to carry on going strong."

While many other major stock markets have hit new highs this year, Tokyo stocks ended their final trading day of the year below their level of a year ago. The Nikkei average closed at 19,361.35, down 7.69 points on the day and around 500 below its 1995 close.

In contrast, the London stock market, Europe's busiest, was aided by a strong opening for futures and bonds. It moved into uncharted territory despite a negative influence of 3.9 points from shares being quoted ex their declared dividend payments.
But traders said share trading volume on both sides of the Atlantic was expected to remain thin with the New Year holiday in the middle of the week.

"I suppose there will be more people around than there were last week but no one wants to get too involved before the New Year's holiday," said one dealer. "There aren't enough people around to make a game."

Since no major British companies are due to report results this week and no major economic data is scheduled, Wall Street, the world's biggest stock market, is likely to be the main market focus, dealers said.
"Christmas sales seem to have rescued retailers but (sales) probably were still below City expectations," one dealer said.
Strength in the dollar -- good news for exporters -- helped encourage the Frankfurt bourse on its final session of the year but some dealers were kept away due to heavy snow.

"This is real end of the year stuff, turnover is thin and everyone is trying to keep clean books. We're also closing early, which won't help volumes, and a lot of people didn't make it because of the snow," said one Frankfurt broker.
French shares took their cue from Wall Street, a stronger franc and higher bond prices but some technical market analysts said the market could slip back later.
Currency traders said the market was concerned whether Japan could sustain its already anaemic economic recovery into 1997, when tax rises will drain funds and public spending will slow.
For traders at work and on the watch for clues on the strength of the U.S. economy, U.S. leading November indicators and existing home sales are due at 1330 and 1500 GMT, respectively.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5545 marks and 115.95 yen, compared with Friday's late European rates of 1.5556 and 115.60.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 18.2 points at 4,109.2.
In Frankfurt the 30-share DAX index was 19.25 higher at 2,872.13. In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 10.25 points at 2,317.20.
On Wall Street the 30-share Dow Jones industrial average rose 14.23 to 6,560.91 on Friday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $369.60 an ounce versus Friday's London close of $369.55. Silver eased one cent to $4.90.
